question: Should ClawHub sign the existing stored hosted feed contract, or approve a new versioned signed feed contract and trust-root rollout?
rationale: Feed signing changes how OpenClaw clients trust ClawHub catalog data, and the current spec says signed envelopes require a separate production key-management decision before advertising them to clients.

options.title: Sign Stored Publications
options.body: Wrap the current stored `catalogFeedPublications` payload with a signature, keep schema v1 exact version/integrity semantics, and document key/trust-root rollout before merge.

options.title: Approve A New Signed Feed
options.body: Accept a new schema/versioned signed feed only after maintainers confirm matching OpenClaw parser support, public routing, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Pause Signing Work
options.body: Leave this draft paused or close it later if the signing RFC, production secret path, and client trust root are not ready to land together.

recommendation.title: Sign Stored Publications
recommendation.body: Wrap the current stored `catalogFeedPublications` payload with a signature, keep schema v1 exact version/integrity semantics, and document key/trust-root rollout before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged hosted-feed work introduced the current feed contract and explicitly split signing into a later production decision.
